string-array.name: tips_library
string-array.item: You can pick several GIFs at once when importing: they are added one after another.
Tap ⋯ on a window to edit, pin as a widget, rename or duplicate the GIF.
Very heavy GIFs look less smooth in a widget. If one is huge, trim it in the editor.
The ▶ button in the bottom bar pauses all your widgets at once.
With battery saver on, widgets pause by themselves. You can change that in Settings.
Short on space? Save the GIF optimized in the editor: it weighs much less.
The buttons at the top switch day and night, music and the background season.
You can switch between the Pixel and Colina XP styles with the little window button below.

string-array.name: tips_editor
string-array.item: Watch the memory counter: if it goes over budget, lower the maximum size or the frames per second.
“Save optimized” makes the GIF ready to use in a widget.
With “Sharp pixels” pixel art stays clean when it is shrunk.
If the GIF has a one-colour background, try the eyedropper to remove it.
Removing frames you do not need saves memory and battery.
Turn on “View original” to compare with the unchanged GIF.

string-array.name: tips_widget
string-array.item: “Fill” covers the whole widget, cropping a little; “Fit” shows the whole GIF with empty bars.
“Auto” picks how to fit the GIF by itself. If you do not like it, try “Fit” or “Fill”.
“Maximum quality” looks better but uses more battery. Use it only on the widget you love most.
A lower speed also saves battery.
You can put a pause button in any corner of the widget.
Tapping the widget can toggle the animation or open the app: choose it below.
